reading.body:
Shaun Taylor is named on 5 AI lobbying filings, all filed through one firm for a single client, THE AI POLICY NETWORK INC., and those filings name 15 separate bills.

The concentration is the story. Five filings, one firm, one client, and 15 bills means the disclosure record describes a single engagement rather than a broad practice. The bills are identified only by number, so the data shows which legislation was touched but not what was said about it, what outcome was sought, or whether the lobbying had any effect.

The disclosed prior position is Deputy Chief of Staff to Rep. Pat Fallon (R-TX). The Lobbying Disclosure Act requires filers to list covered positions held in the prior twenty years, so this is a required disclosure and not an allegation. It is the only biographical fact in the record, and it is the kind of detail that matters for AI policy specifically, because the bills being lobbied are the ones that would set the rules for data centers, model deployment, and federal procurement of AI systems.

What this does not cover: the filings are counted, not read. There is no spending figure, no agency contacted, no text of any communication, and no indication of whether the bills advanced. The record also notes that a different lobbyist shares the name, so the 5 filings belong to LDA lobbyist id 150949 and not to anyone else. Nothing here establishes influence, only registration.

summary: Shaun Taylor is named as a lobbyist on 5 Lobbying Disclosure Act filing(s) about AI held by this site. The firms, clients and AI bills on those filings are below. LDA lobbyist id 150949. A different lobbyist with the same name has a separate page.
